structure.heading: Q1 2026 Loyalty and Satisfaction Performance by Channel (NPS, CSAT, and Effort)
text_content: **Q1 2026 Loyalty and Satisfaction Performance by Channel (NPS, CSAT, and Effort)**

In Q1 2026, overall NPS was 31, CSAT was 84%, and CES was 2.4. These metrics indicate satisfied customers but opportunity to improve loyalty: while CSAT reflects strong transactions, an NPS of 31 shows fewer promoters than desired. The CX organization will prioritize initiatives to convert satisfaction into advocacy across products and services.

In Q1 2026 channel performance diverged sharply: Mobile App NPS was 52 while Phone Support NPS was 12. Mobile App promoters drive referrals and lower support costs; Phone Support shows a disproportionate number of detractors requiring root-cause analysis. Specific actions for Q2 include targeted UX optimization for Mobile App and a focused remediation plan for Phone Support quality and scripting.

Effort data shows Phone Support CES was 3.1 versus Mobile App CES of 2.0 in Q1 2026. Higher phone effort correlates with lower NPS and longer handling times; reducing Phone Support CES should improve loyalty and lower costs. Recommended measures are IVR simplification, first-contact resolution targets, enhanced agent training, and routing traffic to lower-effort Mobile App.

text_content: **Verbatim Sentiment Themes, Journey Pain Points, and a 90-Day Customer Improvement Action Plan**

account confusion (15%), product quality concerns (12%), and agent knowledge gaps (1%0); residual topics included cancellation friction and unclear policy communication. Themes were catgeorized by sentiment and mapped to interaction timestamps and agent IDs to enable targeted coaching, reporting to Customer Service leadership, and prioritization of operational fixes.

5, the highest of all mapped journey points. This pain point correlated with escalations in Email and Social channels and led to repeated agent handoffs during order-status inquiries. Quantitative impact inclueds increased refund requests, late delivery SLA breaches, and elevated churn risk in the 7–30 day window. Recommended next steps include root-cause analysis with Logistics, carrier performance dashboards, prioritized SLA remediation, and targeted carrier cotnract negotiations.

The 90-day Customer Improvement Action Plan begins immediately and targets specific outcomes: NPS increase from 31 to 36 by 30-06-2026 and Phone Support CES reduction from 3.1 to 2.7. Core initiatives: 1) reduce phone wait times via IVR triage, callback scheduling, and workforce reallocation; 2) logistics stabilization sprints to address delivery failure modes and tighten carrier SLAs; 3) agent enablement (knowledge base updates, focused coaching) and weekly CX reporting. Owners: CX Operations, Logistics, Workforce Management; progress will be tracked weekly and reported monthly to the Executive CX Steering Committee.
